maria_finance: FYI — NimbusTech (our channel reseller) filed a claim saying we owe a minimum guarantee (MG) shortfall credit for March. They say contract SVC-2023-NT has a 100k token monthly MG and report shows only 78k tokens billed.

raj_partnerships: ugh. Do we have the signed MG threshold and the measurement method? need to know if we use Marketplace tokens or partner-reported usage.

kevin_nimbus: (from Nimbus) We used the AWS Marketplace metering report and included preview and sandbox tokens per clause 2.1.b. Our calc: 78,342 billable + 21,658 preview = 100,000 -> shortfall claim for the 21,658 tokens.

anna_billing: pulling our recorded marketplace events now. AWS subscription id linked: 9876543210. Quick glance: AWS metering_report.csv shows 78,342 unit_usage for Mar. We do NOT count preview/sandbox as billable per our onboarding note for Nimbus.

billing-bot: :warning: Discrepancy detected between partner-reported usage and platform meter for subscription 9876543210. Flagged for manual review.

maria_finance: OK — two separate issues: (1) measurement source mismatch, (2) contract interpretation. Tomas, can legal confirm clause language?

Tomas_legal: clause 2.1.b in SVC-2023-NT: "Billable units shall exclude non-production preview and sandbox usage unless explicitly designated as billable in Appendix A." Appendix A is blank. So the contract supports us not counting preview tokens.

raj_partnerships: good. Ask Nimbus for their raw AWS CSV and a quick calc showing which rows they're treating as preview. If they can't map rows to our metering IDs we escalate.

kevin_nimbus: attaching our export now: https://files.nimbustech.co/reports/mar-export.csv. We highlighted preview rows in column "usage_type" but happy to map to metering ids.

anna_billing: I pulled their file, did a diff vs our AWS metering: most of the extra 21k are "preview_session" entries that have a different usage_dimension (preview_tokens). Those do not appear in our billable dimension. Snippet:

```
invoice_line: subscription 9876543210, dimension text_generation.tokens, 78342
invoice_line: subscription 9876543210, dimension preview.tokens, 21658
```

maria_finance: So the reconciliation looks straightforward — partner included preview tokens. We need Nimbus to sign off to remove the shortfall claim. Action items: (a) ask Nimbus to withdraw claim or refile with billable rows only, (b) if they refuse, we prepare a formal response referencing clause 2.1.b and attach reconciled CSV.

kevin_nimbus: Nimbus prefers a credit rather than refile. Is there wiggle room for a goodwill credit? We lost trust with their sales team.

maria_finance: From finance POV: we can offer a one-time goodwill gesture but need approvals. Estimate of credit = (21,658 tokens * unit_rate). Anna, what's the unit_rate used for Nimbus in Mar?

anna_billing: unit_rate = $0.0005 per token for their tier -> provisional credit = $10.829 (rounded $10.83). Small amount but contractual principle matters.

raj_partnerships: If it's $10.83 and Nimbus wants to preserve relationship maybe approve as one-off. But loop in Tomas for any contractual concession.

Tomas_legal: I'm fine with a one-time goodwill credit under these facts as long as we document that this is not precedent and update onboarding docs. I'll draft the email language.

maria_finance: Great. Final plan: (1) Maria to send draft response with reconciled CSV and clause excerpt, offering either (A) withdraw claim (preferred) or (B) one-time goodwill credit of $10.83 with signed waiver. (2) Anna to attach reconciled CSV and meter diff. (3) Raj to confirm relationship note/why we make exception. (4) Close within 3 business days.

kevin_nimbus: Appreciate the quick handling. We'll review the draft and get back by EOD. :v:

anna_billing: uploading reconciled CSV to our share: https://redwood.s3/reconciliations/nimbus_mar_recon.csv

maria_finance: sending draft now. cc @tomas_legal. will post update in this thread after Nimbus responds. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: action_required: credit_request_reviewed by maria_finance. status: pending-approval."
